name: Congenital Pulmonary Veins Anomaly

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Pulmonary Veins Anomaly Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Identification of pulmonary veins draining into systemic venous circulation or abnormal sites
Evidence of pulmonary venous obstruction or stenosis on imaging
Presence of cyanosis, respiratory distress, or heart failure symptoms in neonate or infant

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anomalous pulmonary vein connection confirmed by imaging plus at least one clinical or imaging supportive criterion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities such as echocardiography, CT angiography, or MRI.

pathognomonic.notes: Central cyanosis often present in neonates
searchTerms: blue skin from abnormal heart blood flow
cyanosis due to right-to-left heart shunt

common.notes: Common in infants with significant venous obstruction
Due to chronic hypoxia and cardiac insufficiency

occasional.notes: Rare but may occur due to venous hypertension

searchTerms: nerve deficits caused by low oxygen

laboratory: Elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating anomalous pulmonary venous return
CT angiography or MRI confirming pulmonary vein anatomy and obstruction
Chest X-ray showing pulmonary venous congestion
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; may be sporadic or associated with congenital heart disease syndromes
other: Cardiac catheterization may be used for hemodynamic assessment and confirmation

distinguishingFeatures: All pulmonary veins drain anomalously with obligatory right-to-left shunting
Usually presents with severe cyanosis and heart failure in neonates
Only some pulmonary veins drain anomalously
Often less severe symptoms and may present later in childhood
Narrowing of pulmonary veins without anomalous connection
Progressive pulmonary hypertension and respiratory symptoms

redFlags: Severe cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Progressive respiratory distress and heart failure in neonate
Pulmonary venous obstruction causing pulmonary hypertension
references: Gatzoulis MA, et al. Diagnosis and Management of Anomalous Pulmonary Venous Connections. Heart. 2017.
Orphanet: Congenital Pulmonary Veins Anomaly. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
Mavroudis C, Backer CL. Pediatric Cardiac Surgery. 4th Edition. 2013.
